clue.text: Troublesome furniture-remover gets politer after treatment

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are worked over, as a patient is after treatment, into a new order

explanation.surface: A grumpy removal man becomes more courteous once he has been dealt with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Troublesome furniture-remover' sounds like a bad removal man; it describes a spirit that throws furniture about.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy spirit is blamed for throwing and shifting household objects about, hence a mischievous mover of furniture.

clue.text: Mountain-nymph has nothing to say

parts.note: nothing is zero, which looks like the letter O
to read is to say what is written, as a notice reads 'Keep out'

explanation.surface: A nymph of the hills is silent, with nothing to contribute.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the oreads were the nymphs who lived in mountains and grottoes.

clue.text: Sting I'd treat with dispatch

indicators.note: to treat the letters is to process them into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to deal promptly with a stinging insect or a jab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispatch' looks like a verb meaning to deal with quickly, but it is the noun: a dispatch is a news report.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispatch is a report or message sent from afar, so news brought in.

clue.text: Deliver salvage free and save lives?

explanation.surface: A lifeboat crew's job: deliver, salvage, liberate and preserve lives.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions in a row; the last, with its question mark, describes the answer as what lifeguards do.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver, to salvage and to free people from danger all mean to save them from harm.

clue.text: The Mount", correct address of cardinal?

explanation.surface: A note on the proper way to greet a cardinal at his residence, The Mount.
explanation.walkthrough: His or Her Eminence is the formal style for a cardinal of the Roman Catholic Church.
explanation.definitionFit: A mount is a height or hill, and a cardinal is formally styled His Eminence.

clue.text: Tess of the D'Urbevilles opening can be the most tender

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase can be made into another word, so they are rearranged
the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the opening of the title words 'the D'Urbervilles' is its first letter, T

explanation.surface: The start of Hardy's Tess of the D'Urbervilles can be the most moving part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' rearranges TESS, OF and T (the opening of 'the D'Urbevilles') into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Most tender means gentlest or softest to the touch or heart.

clue.text: Noted fun in Oklahoma, for example

parts.note: noted here means set to musical notes, so tuneful
fun is entertainment that makes people laugh, a comedy

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on the fun to be had in the state of Oklahoma.
explanation.walkthrough: Oklahoma! is a Rodgers and Hammerstein stage show, not just the US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Oklahoma! is a famous light-hearted stage show with songs, the classic example of the genre.

clue.text: Burns left on the head from brown coals

indicators.note: placed on the head of the next piece, so it comes at the front

parts.note: burns means catches fire, ignites

explanation.surface: Robert Burns appears with the head turned leftwards, drawn from brown coal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burns' looks like the Scottish poet but is the verb, ignites.
explanation.definitionFit: Lignite is a soft brownish coal, between peat and bituminous coal.

clue.text: Actors sport in new comic pictures

indicators.note: a new arrangement of the letters is called for

explanation.surface: Performers show off in some fresh funny drawings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' tells you to rearrange ACTORS SPORT IN together.
explanation.definitionFit: Comic pictures are cartoons laid out in a sequence of panels across a page.

clue.text: To affect drastically at university, finish last

indicators.note: this piece comes last, after the other

parts.note: UP means in residence at university, as in 'up at Oxford'
a finish is an end

explanation.surface: A student at university finishing last is badly shaken.
explanation.definitionFit: To upend something is to turn it upside down, figuratively to overturn it completely.

clue.text: Scrooge fell approaching Welsh town

indicators.note: the first piece comes up to the second, so it goes before it

parts.note: a fell is an animal's hide or pelt
Flint is a town in north-east Wales

explanation.surface: A miser stumbles while nearing a town in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' looks like the past of fall, but it is the noun meaning hide. Ebenezer Scrooge is Dickens's miser.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrooge, from Dickens's A Christmas Carol, stands for any mean, money-hoarding person.

clue.text: Contract drawn up, wearing false smile?

parts.note: in means dressed in or wearing, as in 'in a suit'
a set of false teeth gives an artificial smile

explanation.surface: An agreement is drafted while someone puts on an insincere grin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'false smile' suggests insincerity, but here it is literal: dentures are false teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: An indenture is a formal written agreement, historically binding an apprentice to a master.

clue.text: Listlessness a bit of a rotten nuisance

indicators.note: only a portion of the phrase is used, a run of letters inside it

explanation.surface: Lethargy is a small part of what makes a nuisance so rotten.
explanation.definitionFit: Listlessness is weariness from boredom, a French-borrowed word for tedium.

clue.text: As good as resort of St Malo

indicators.note: re-sort, sorting the letters afresh into a new order

explanation.surface: St Malo is described as practically a resort town on the Brittany coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday town, which St Malo is, but read as re-sort it rearranges ST MALO.
explanation.definitionFit: As good as means nearly or very nearly, a synonym.

clue.text: One's marbles reduced without thinking

parts.note: one's marbles is slang for one's wits or mental faculties
reduced means made smaller, less

explanation.surface: Someone's marbles are fewer, so they act foolishly.
explanation.definitionFit: Mindless means acting without thought or intelligence.

clue.text: City area still euphoric?

parts.note: EC is the postcode district of the City of London
still means motionless, static

explanation.surface: Is a part of the city that stays quiet actually delighted?
explanation.walkthrough: EC (East Central) covers London's financial district, the City.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphoric means intensely happy, overjoyed.

clue.text: State of young girl, beautiful girl who loses head

parts.note: a miss is a young unmarried girl

indicators.note: the beautiful girl loses her head, the first letter of the word

parts.note: a houri is a beautiful maiden of the Islamic paradise

explanation.surface: A young girl's condition is described as that of a beauty who panics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a condition but is a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Missouri is one of the states of the USA, in the Midwest.

clue.text: Pot and tin basin damaged

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: the word basin is knocked out of shape, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A cooking pot, a tin and a basin are all damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges BASIN into NABIS. 'Pot' is the drug, not the cooking vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Pot is slang for marijuana, the drug from the hemp plant.

clue.text: Type of camel associated with the M1 at night?

definitions.text: Type of camel associated with the M1 at night?

parts.words: Type of camel associated with the M1 at night?
parts.note: M1 is Roman M (a thousand) plus one, linking the camel breed to the Thousand and One Nights tales

explanation.surface: Someone wonders which camel would be seen on the motorway after dark.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a British motorway, but read as Roman numerals it is 1001, as in The Thousand and One Nights, also known by the camel's breed name.
explanation.definitionFit: The dromedary is the one-humped camel of that breed, and the Thousand and One Nights stories share its name.

clue.text: Mad search for a drink.

indicators.note: mad suggests wild disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A frantic hunt for something to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaser is a drink taken straight after another, such as a beer after a spirit.

clue.text: Wretched Henry, a penny down

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
down means short by, less, as in 'down a pound'

explanation.surface: Poor Henry finds himself a penny short.
explanation.definitionFit: Hapless means unlucky and unfortunate.

clue.text: Peg price, say, of wall decoration

indicators.note: say indicates that the word is pronounced, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: to peg a price is to fix it, to freeze it

explanation.surface: Someone asks the cost of a peg for hanging wall decorations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peg' looks like a noun but is a verb: to peg prices is to freeze them.
explanation.definitionFit: A frieze is a decorative horizontal band along the top of a wall.

clue.text: … one following whisky in a holiday island

indicators.note: this piece comes after the other

parts.note: malt is a malt whisky
a means one, as in 'a pound'

explanation.surface: Continuing a previous clue: a dram of whisky on a Mediterranean holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading ellipsis just links the surface to the clue before; it has no job in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Malta is a Mediterranean island country popular with tourists.

clue.text: Dropping the subject of punishment

parts.note: read as letting a victim fall on a rope as torture, not as abandoning a topic

explanation.surface: Someone changes the conversation away from discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subject' seems to be a topic, but it is the person subjected to the torture, hoisted by the wrists and dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Strappado was a torture in which the victim was hoisted by a rope and jerked by being let fall.

clue.text: Bill Hill — figure in Whitehall, perhaps

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A man called Bill Hill is a civil servant in Whitehall.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitehall suggests the civil service, but the Whitehall Theatre in London was famous for farces, so a figure there is a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer on the stage of the Whitehall Theatre, home of London farce, would be a player in its shows.

clue.text: Test due? It may be very poor

indicators.note: the letters may be formed into something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A student wonders whether an imminent exam will go very badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very poor' looks like a verdict on the test but defines the answer, penniless.
explanation.definitionFit: Destitute means lacking the basic necessities of life, utterly impoverished.

clue.text: Whipped, with head removed, and swallowed

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: whipped means beaten, as eggs or a defeated side

explanation.surface: A dish is whipped, decapitated and gulped down.
explanation.definitionFit: Swallowed food has been consumed, gulped down.

clue.text: Nervy, as rain breaks out for the celebration

indicators.note: the letters break out of their order and form a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A tense guest frets as rain starts falling on the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks out' rearranges NERVY AS RAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: An anniversary is the yearly return of a date that is celebrated, such as a wedding.
